# Task Launch Policy

An abstract Connected Clause marker for policies that invoke the package-owned Work request function. This type supplies no launch action body, task lifecycle or completion guarantee. Its inherited connection machinery determines when declared actions may run; requesting work does not confirm that work started or completed.

## Configuration

`parameters.workClause` defaults to `"work"`. The supplied definitions do not show how the Work request function consumes this parameter or how changing it affects routing. No required-value validation for it is shown.

`bindingTypes` is empty, so this marker declares no data bindings. Inherited action bindings associate declared action names with dictionaries of named connections. Executable actions and hooks come from the admitted exact clause type. Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no dot, slash or tilde. Transition validation rejects a changed clause under its existing key with `CONNECTIONS_REQUIRE_NEW_CLAUSE_KEY`.

## Inherited connection behavior

Where actions are declared, connections can use `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `initialized`, `activated` or `timer` sources. `initialized` observes Clauses Initialized; `activated` observes Document Activated. Workflow connections require an authenticated channel binding, selected by `party` when supplied, otherwise `channel`. This does not establish the current viewer's permission or a personal obligation.

Action `defaults` are merged with connection `params`. A false connection `when` skips execution; it defaults to true. Declared `args` must satisfy their argument pattern. Action `require.when` and the corresponding `parameters.conditions` entry must pass or the attempt fails. Conditions naming an unknown action are rejected.

Execution proceeds through optional `preflight`, connection `before`, action `do`, and connection `after`. A declared preflight must set `actionResult.outcome` to `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` proceeds to `before` and `do`. An action using `resultContract: "outcome-v1"` must likewise provide one of those outcomes after `do`; only `acceptedNew` proceeds to `after` and the final once marker. These are action-processing outcomes, not confirmation of external Work completion.

`once` defaults to false. When true, an already marked connection skips subsequent execution. Its marker is written only after the action passes the applicable outcome checks and `after` finishes.

Timer connections require exactly one of `timestamp` or `afterEvent`. An absolute `timestamp` is an integer Unix-microsecond deadline from 0 through 9007199254740991 and cannot use `delayMs` or `policy`. An `afterEvent` timer requires a timestamped source and a positive integer `delayMs` no greater than 9007199254740. Its `policy` defaults to `first`, which suppresses further arming once marked armed; `latest` allows replacement of the pending keyed timer. Optional `cancelOn` emits a cancellation request. Committed requests require the Time runtime: emission is not firing, and cancellation cannot undo an earlier firing.

## Connection state

The inherited planner supplies `armed: false` and `fired: false` for each connection under `/connectionState_{clauseKey}`, keyed by the joined action and connection names. Missing state is unknown, not an initialized false value.

`armed` records timer arming. Neither cancellation nor firing clears it in the supplied implementation, so it is not a current pending-timer indicator; a cancelled `first` timer remains blocked from rearming by this flag. `fired` records reaching the final marker of a `once` connection, not task completion or every timer firing. Connections without `once` do not set it through this execution path. No Work request status, task result or task completion date is established by these flags.
